environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; python raw-socket probes, curl 8.18.0 cross-check

findings.description: pathnorm rejects only NUL and backslash, so CR and LF from the request path survive into the location string, and response() concatenates that string into the head verbatim. GET /hdr%0d%0aX-Inject:%20yes yields a real X-Inject: yes/ line; a Set-Cookie payload installs a live cookie; CRLFCRLF ends the head early and turns the genuine tail into body; a forged Content-Length produces a duplicate that fails curl with Invalid Content-Length. Precondition: an attacker-chosen path segment on this build, and a directory whose name contains the control bytes. It is a client-side response-splitting primitive, not server-side execution.
findings.title: The 301 Location is concatenated into the header block from the decoded path while the path decoder admits CR and LF, so the response head can be split and headers forged

limitations: Static build: no upstream, so nothing executes on the server
Injected header lines carry a trailing slash and any query because the target is a slashless directory
